scenario: 45 分钟的 Twitter 设计面结束时，白板上组件不少，但没有一条请求能端到端跑通。
scenario_en: At the end of a 45-minute Twitter design, the board is full of boxes but no request can actually run end to end.
q: 中级候选人挂掉系统设计面试最常见的原因是？
options: 算 QPS/DAU 时出了算术错误
选用了不够『潮』的数据库
没能交付出一个可运行的完整系统
白板图画得不够美观
options_en: Made an arithmetic mistake estimating QPS or DAU.
Picked a database that felt unfashionable.
Failed to deliver a working, complete system.
The whiteboard diagram wasn't pretty enough.
why: 最容易自毁的方式是没能交付出可工作的系统；这是中级候选人最常见的挂点，表面上常被误诊为『时间管理』问题。
why_en: The single easiest way to fail is not delivering a working system, which mid-level candidates most often misdiagnose as a time-management problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统每秒处理的查询次数，衡量负载的常用单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS is the number of queries a system handles per second, a standard load metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每天实际使用产品的独立用户数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU is the count of unique users who use the product on a given day.

q_en: What is the most common reason mid-level candidates fail system design interviews?
optionExplanations: 算术小错通常能当场纠正，不是真正压垮候选人的原因。
数据库选型见仁见智，考官通常能接受，不是致命伤。
对，真正压垮候选人的是设计始终没能拼成一套端到端跑得通的系统。
画面好不好看从不是评分项，考官在意的是逻辑而非配色。
optionExplanations_en: A small arithmetic slip is usually fixable on the spot, not the real failure point.
Database taste is debatable and interviewers usually accept several choices, so it is rarely fatal.
Right — what actually sinks candidates is never assembling a system that runs end to end.
Tidiness was never scored; interviewers judge logic, not how pretty the diagram looks.

scenario: 你需求和 API 都讲得很细，等开始画高层设计时只剩 5 分钟，复盘被记成「时间管理差」。
scenario_en: You covered requirements and the API in depth, then had five minutes left for high-level design, and the debrief called it poor time management.
q: 所谓「时间管理差」的真相通常是什么？
options: 不是要快一倍，而是要把时间花对地方
确实需要把说话语速练得更快
是这场面试分配的时间本身就不够用
是面试官计时工具本身不准确
options_en: It's not about working twice as fast, but focusing on the right things.
You really do need to talk faster.
The interview simply doesn't allocate enough time.
The interviewer's timing is inaccurate.
why: 问题往往不是速度，而是聚焦：把精力放在考官最看重的部分，就不需要『工作快两倍』。
why_en: The issue is rarely that you must work twice as fast; usually you just need to focus on the right things.
q_en: What is the real issue behind so-called poor time management?
optionExplanations: 对，慢的真正原因通常是没聚焦重点，而不是手速不够快。
语速只是表面症状，说得快不会让设计更完整，反而更乱。
45 分钟对所有人一视同仁，抱怨时间不够解决不了问题。
计时误差不会系统性地拖垮候选人，别把锅甩给工具。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the usual cause of 'slow' is missing focus, not needing to move faster.
Talking faster is a surface symptom; it won't make the design more complete, just messier.
Everyone gets the same forty-five minutes, so blaming the clock doesn't fix anything.
Timing error isn't a systematic cause of failure — don't blame the tool.

scenario: 第一次真刀真枪的 45 分钟设计面，你一被追问就容易断片，需要一条能退回去的固定轨道。
scenario_en: It is your first real 45-minute design loop and you freeze under follow-ups, so you want a fixed track you can fall back to.
q: 跟随交付框架（Delivery Framework）的好处有哪些？（多选）
options: 始终聚焦在面试官最看重的部分
紧张、被问懵时有清晰的回退路径
线性搭建方案，不容易迷路、不容易卡死
保证一定拿到 offer
options_en: Keeps you focused on what the interviewer cares about most.
Gives you a clear fallback path when you freeze up under nerves.
Builds the solution linearly, so you rarely get lost or stuck.
Guarantees you'll get the offer.
why: 框架 = 一套推荐的步骤与时间分配：让你聚焦重点、慌乱时有轨道可退、并线性搭建方案——但它不是 offer 保票。
why_en: The framework keeps you focused on what matters, gives you a track to fall back on when nervous, and helps you build the solution linearly.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    F["Framework"] --> P["Focus"]
    F --> R["Fallback path"]
    F --> C["Complete system"]
q_en: What are the benefits of following the Delivery Framework? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 锚定注意力在考官最看重的部分，省掉临场判断该讲什么的成本。
紧张或被问懵时有固定步骤可退守，不会当场卡死。
按顺序搭建方案，减少同时改十个地方、推倒重来的风险。
误把有方法论当成必过，框架买的是节奏，不是结果。
optionExplanations_en: Anchors your attention on what interviewers score, cutting the cost of deciding what to cover next.
Gives you fixed steps to fall back on when you freeze up, so you don't stall mid-interview.
Builds the solution step by step, cutting the risk of touching ten things at once and redoing work.
Mistakes having a method for a guaranteed pass — the framework buys pacing, not the offer.

scenario: 面试只有 35-45 分钟。按 Hello Interview 的 Delivery Framework，你要在开口前决定每个环节大概花多久，才不会前面磨蹭、后面来不及深挖。
q: 补全交付框架各环节的建议用时：
text: 需求 ~{{5}} 分钟 → 核心实体 ~{{2}} 分钟 → API ~{{5}} 分钟 →（可选：数据流 ~5 分钟）→ 高层设计 ~{{10-15}} 分钟 → 深挖 ~{{10}} 分钟。
why: 这是 Hello Interview Delivery Framework 的建议预算，高层设计占比最大。数字不用死记，用途是提醒「需求和实体别磨太久，把时间留给深挖」；不同公司和面试官节奏会有出入。
why_en: This is Hello Interview's suggested Delivery Framework budget, with high-level design taking the largest share. The point is not the exact minutes but protecting deep-dive time; pacing varies by company and interviewer.
q_en: Fill in the recommended time budget for each Delivery Framework stage:
scenario_en: The interview is only 35 to 45 minutes. Following Hello Interview's Delivery Framework, set a rough time budget for each stage before you start, so you don't stall early and lose the deep-dive window.
text_en: Requirements ~{{5}} min → Core entities ~{{2}} min → API ~{{5}} min → (optional: data flow ~5 min) → High-level design ~{{10-15}} min → Deep dives ~{{10}} min.

q: 把交付框架的五个主环节按面试推进顺序排列：
steps: 高层设计（画框图，逐个 endpoint 搭建）
需求（功能性 + 非功能性）
深挖（加固设计以满足非功能需求）
API 或系统接口（定义契约）
核心实体（列出系统的关键名词）
why: 需求 → 核心实体 → API → 高层设计 → 深挖；数据处理型系统可在 API 后插入可选的『数据流』环节。
why_en: The delivery framework runs requirements, core entities, API, high-level design, and finally deep dives, with an optional data-flow step for data-processing systems.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R["需求 ~5min"] --> E["核心实体 ~2min"]
    E --> A["API ~5min"]
    A -.-> D["数据流（可选）~5min"]
    A --> H["高层设计 ~10-15min"]
    D -.-> H
    H --> DD["深挖 ~10min"]
q_en: Put the five main Delivery Framework stages in interview order:

scenario: 45 分钟设计 Twitter，需求环节只有 ~5 分钟，你要用一句固定句式把核心功能写上白板。
scenario_en: You have about five minutes of requirements time in a Twitter design, so you need one fixed sentence pattern for core features.
q: 功能性需求（functional requirements）的标准句式是？
options: "The system should be..."（系统整体应当具备的品质）
"Users/Clients should be able to..."
"We will use..."（我们打算采用的实现方式）
"The database must..."（数据库层面必须满足）
options_en: "The system should be..."
"Users/Clients should be able to..."
"We will use..."
"The database must..."
why: 功能需求描述系统的核心特性，句式是『用户/客户端应能做 X』；它是需求环节第一个要跟考官对齐的内容。
why_en: Functional requirements are the "users should be able to" statements that capture the core features of the system.
q_en: What is the standard phrasing for a functional requirement?
optionExplanations: 这是非功能需求的句式，描述系统品质而不是用户动作。
对，这正是功能需求的标准句式——描述用户能做的具体动作。
这是技术选型的表态，不是在描述需求。
这是对某个组件下的约束，不是面向用户的需求陈述。
optionExplanations_en: This phrasing describes a system quality, i.e. a non-functional requirement, not a feature.
Right — this is the standard functional-requirement phrasing, naming a concrete user action.
This states an implementation choice, not a requirement at all.
This constrains one component rather than stating what the user can do.

scenario: 题目只有一句「设计一个 Twitter」，需求环节 ~5 分钟，考官在等你决定哪些功能进范围。
scenario_en: The prompt is just "design Twitter", you have about five minutes, and the interviewer is waiting on you to scope it.
q: 收集功能需求的正确姿势是？
options: 独自把想到的功能列完，最后一次性甩给考官
被动等待面试官主动报需求
把题目原文照抄一遍当需求
像产品经理一样提针对性问题，对齐优先级
options_en: List every feature you can think of on your own, then hand the whole set to the interviewer at once.
Passively wait for the interviewer to hand you the requirements.
Copy the prompt's wording verbatim as your requirements.
Ask targeted questions like a product manager and align priorities with the interviewer.
why: 需求环节常是与考官的 back-and-forth：用针对性提问逼出核心功能，并排出优先级。
why_en: Gather functional requirements by asking targeted questions as if talking to a product manager, iterating with the interviewer toward a prioritized feature list.
q_en: What is the right way to gather functional requirements?
optionExplanations: 把需求收集当成一个人闷头完成的任务，跳过了和考官对齐的环节。
把主动权完全交给考官，自己不驱动对话，容易冷场。
只是把已知信息复述一遍，没有产出任何新判断。
对，用针对性提问像产品经理一样逼出核心功能并排优先级。
optionExplanations_en: Treats gathering requirements as a solo task, skipping the alignment step with the interviewer.
Hands all initiative to the interviewer instead of driving the conversation, which stalls it.
Just restates what's already known without adding any new judgment.
Right — ask targeted questions like a product manager to surface features and rank priority.

scenario: 真实产品（如 Twitter、Amazon）动辄有上百个功能，但 45 分钟的面试不可能把它们都设计一遍。
q: 面对上百个真实功能，你应该识别并聚焦前几个核心功能？
options: 10 个以上，尽量全
前 3 个左右
只挑 1 个
全部列出再筛选
options_en: Ten or more, aim for full coverage.
Roughly the top three.
Just one feature.
List every single one, then filter.
why: 你的职责是从上百个功能里挑出并优先处理 top 3 左右；这份小清单撑起接下来整场面试的设计，多了拖慢节奏、少了撑不起系统。
why_en: Your job is to identify and prioritize roughly the top three core features out of the hundreds the real product has, since that short list has to carry the rest of the interview.
q_en: When a real product has hundreds of features, how many core features should you focus on?
scenario_en: Real products like Twitter or Amazon have hundreds of features, but a 45-minute interview cannot design all of them.
optionExplanations: 10 个以上会稀释深挖环节的火力，撑不起 45 分钟该有的深度。
对，挑出 top 3 左右，用这份小清单撑起接下来整场设计。
只挑 1 个功能又太单薄，撑不起一个完整系统该有的复杂度。
全列再筛看似严谨，实际上会先耗光本该留给设计的时间。
optionExplanations_en: Ten-plus features dilute the deep-dive time you need later in the interview.
Right — pick roughly the top three; that short list has to carry the rest of the design.
Just one feature is too thin to support a full system's worth of design.
Listing everything before filtering looks thorough but burns time you need for the design.

scenario: 45 分钟设计 Twitter，你在需求环节列了 12 条功能，后面还要画完设计并留出深挖。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute Twitter design you listed twelve features up front, and you still have to build the design and leave room for deep dives.
q: 把功能需求列得又长又全的后果是？
options: 弊大于利，大厂直接评估聚焦重点的能力
显得准备充分，考官通常会因此给你加分
对后续设计完全没有任何影响
可以直接跳过深挖环节不做了
options_en: It backfires — top companies directly evaluate your ability to focus.
It looks thorough, so the interviewer usually gives you bonus points.
It has no effect on the rest of the design.
It lets you skip the deep-dives step entirely.
why: 长清单会拖垮后面所有环节；不少 FAANG 把『能否聚焦最重要的事』作为直接评估项。
why_en: A long requirements list hurts more than it helps, since top companies directly evaluate your ability to focus on what matters.
q_en: What happens if you list every possible functional requirement?
optionExplanations: 对，长清单会被考官当成不会取舍的负面信号，拖慢后续每一步。
看起来认真，实际考官反而会追问哪个最重要，暴露你没做取舍。
需求环节和后面的 API、设计并不独立，臃肿清单会拖慢它们。
详略只在需求环节，深挖仍要单独跑一遍，省不掉。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a long list reads as a negative signal for prioritization and slows every step after it.
It looks thorough, but interviewers will instead ask which one matters most, exposing no prioritization.
Requirements aren't independent from what follows; a bloated list slows the API and design too.
Detail here doesn't buy anything back — deep dives still have to run on their own.

scenario: 45 分钟设计 Twitter，需求环节只够写三条功能，必须挑出撑得起整套设计的那几条。
scenario_en: You only have room for three functional requirements in a 45-minute Twitter design, so they must be the ones the whole design hangs on.
q: 设计 Twitter 时合理的核心功能需求有哪些？（多选）
options: 用户应能发推文
用户应能关注其他用户
用户应能看到所关注用户的推文
用户应能购买广告位
options_en: Users should be able to post tweets.
Users should be able to follow other users.
Users should be able to see tweets from users they follow.
Users should be able to purchase ad placements.
why: 发推、关注、看关注流是 Twitter 的 top 3 核心功能；广告投放不是面试 45 分钟里该抓的重点。
why_en: For Twitter the core functional requirements are posting tweets, following users, and seeing tweets from followed users.
q_en: Which core functional requirements are reasonable for designing Twitter? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 发推是最基本的写路径，没有它整个系统没有内容来源。
关注定义了用户间的图关系，feed 靠它决定该展示谁的内容。
看关注流是发推之后的核心读路径，是发推和关注共同的出口。
广告投放涉及独立的计费和竞价系统，不是 45 分钟该抓的核心。
optionExplanations_en: Posting is the most basic write path — without it there's no content source at all.
Following defines the graph between users; the feed relies on it to know whose content to show.
Viewing the feed is the core read path after posting, the output both writes feed into.
Ad placement pulls in a separate billing and bidding system, not core to a 45-minute design.

scenario: Twitter 的功能需求已经对齐，考官接着问「这套系统还该满足什么」，要写第二类需求。
scenario_en: The functional requirements are agreed, and the interviewer asks what else the system has to satisfy.
q: 非功能性需求（non-functional requirements，NFR）描述的是什么？
options: 系统要实现的功能清单
团队的开发流程
对用户重要的系统品质
运维值班安排
options_en: The list of features the system must implement.
The team's development process.
System qualities that matter to users.
The on-call rotation schedule.
why: 非功能需求刻画系统品质：可用性、扩展性、延迟等，句式是 "The system should (be able to)..."。
why_en: Non-functional requirements are statements about system qualities that matter to users, phrased as "the system should be" statements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 刻画系统品质（延迟/可用性/扩展性等）而非具体动作的需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A non-functional requirement describes a system quality like latency or availability, not a user action.

q_en: What do non-functional requirements, or NFRs, describe?
optionExplanations: 这其实是功能需求的定义，不是非功能需求。
团队开发流程是管理话题，和系统品质无关。
对，非功能需求就是刻画延迟、可用性这类对用户重要的系统品质。
运维值班安排属于组织话题，不属于需求环节。
optionExplanations_en: This is actually the definition of a functional requirement, not a non-functional one.
Team process is a management topic, unrelated to system qualities.
Right — NFRs describe system qualities like latency and availability that matter to users.
On-call scheduling is an organizational topic, not part of requirements gathering.

scenario: 设计 Twitter feed，你在 NFR 里写了一句「系统应该低延迟」，考官追问「多低？哪一段？」
scenario_en: You wrote "the system should be low latency" as a non-functional requirement for the Twitter feed, and the interviewer asks how low and where.
q: 「系统应该低延迟」这条非功能需求的问题在哪？
options: 延迟根本不属于非功能需求
太空泛，需结合语境量化
这样写没问题，直接照抄即可
低延迟只和前端渲染有关
options_en: Latency isn't even a non-functional requirement.
It's too vague; it should be scoped and quantified.
It's fine as written; just copy it in as-is.
Low latency only concerns front-end rendering.
why: 好的 NFR 要放进系统语境并尽量量化：指出最需要低延迟的部分、给出目标值，否则这句话没有信息量。
why_en: Saying the system should be low latency is meaningless; a useful requirement names the part that matters and quantifies it, like search under 500 milliseconds.
q_en: What is wrong with saying only that the system should have low latency?
optionExplanations: 延迟其实是最典型的非功能需求之一，把它排除在外才是错的。
对，问题在于太空泛——好的 NFR 要放进语境并尽量量化。
模板句直接照抄没有信息量，深挖环节没法验收它。
延迟不只是前端的事，后端查询和网络传输同样贡献延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Latency is actually one of the most typical NFRs, so excluding it is the real mistake.
Right — the problem is vagueness; a useful NFR needs to be scoped and quantified.
Copying the template sentence as-is gives nothing checkable during deep dives.
Latency isn't only a front-end concern — backend queries and network hops add it too.

q: 补全 Twitter 的非功能需求示例：
text: 系统应高可用，{{可用性}}优先于{{一致性}}；应能扩展到支撑 100M+ 日活用户；feed 渲染{{延迟}}应低于 200ms。
why: 题面说「晚几秒可以、打不开不行」，就是在分区时选可用性、接受最终一致；200ms 是对 feed 渲染延迟的量化目标。三条示范了 NFR 的写法：点名 CAP 取舍、给规模数字、给量化延迟——每条都能在深挖环节被验收。
why_en: "A few seconds late is fine, failing to load is not" means choosing availability over consistency during partitions and accepting eventual consistency; 200 ms is a quantified latency target for feed rendering. Together they show how to write NFRs: name the CAP trade-off, give a scale number, and give a measurable latency target.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统在网络分区时只能同时保证一致性与可用性中的一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can guarantee only consistency or availability, not both, during a network partition.

q_en: Fill in the Twitter non-functional requirement examples:
scenario: 设计 Twitter，功能需求已对齐。产品方明确：新推文晚几秒才出现在粉丝 feed 里可以接受，但 feed 不能打不开；目标规模 100M+ 日活，feed 渲染延迟目标 200ms 以内。请把它写成非功能需求。
scenario_en: You are designing Twitter and the functional requirements are agreed. Product says a new tweet may take a few seconds to reach followers' feeds, but the feed must never fail to load; the target is 100M+ daily active users and feed rendering under 200 ms. Write these as non-functional requirements.
text_en: The system should be highly available, prioritizing {{availability}} over {{consistency}}; it should scale to 100M+ DAU; feed rendering {{latency}} should be under 200 ms.

scenario: 45 分钟设计面，NFR 环节只够写 3-5 条，你要从一份通用清单里挑最贴本系统的维度。
scenario_en: You only have room for three to five non-functional requirements, so you pick from a standard checklist the ones this system actually cares about.
q: 非功能需求检查清单中包含哪些维度？（多选）
options: CAP 取舍与环境约束（电池/内存/带宽）
扩展性（突发流量、读写比）与延迟
持久性、安全、容错、合规
团队人数与代码风格
options_en: CAP trade-off and environment constraints (battery, memory, bandwidth).
Scalability (bursty traffic, read/write ratio) and latency.
Durability, security, fault tolerance, compliance.
Team headcount and coding style.
why: 清单共八项：CAP、环境约束、扩展性、延迟、持久性、安全、容错、合规——从中挑出与本系统最相关的 3-5 条。
why_en: The checklist covers CAP trade-offs, environment constraints, scalability, latency, durability, security, fault tolerance, and compliance.
q_en: Which dimensions belong in the non-functional requirement checklist? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 覆盖分布式取舍与运行环境的物理限制，比如移动端的电池和带宽。
覆盖流量形状和响应速度，决定该扩读还是扩写、要不要扛峰值。
覆盖数据能不能丢、故障能不能扛住、合不合规这三类风险。
团队人数和代码风格属于组织管理，不改变系统架构本身。
optionExplanations_en: Covers distributed trade-offs and physical limits, like a mobile app's battery and bandwidth.
Covers traffic shape and response speed, deciding whether to scale reads, writes, or absorb spikes.
Covers whether data can be lost, failures survived, or compliance rules met.
Headcount and coding style are organizational, and don't change the architecture itself.

scenario: Twitter 跨多机房部署，网络分区必然发生；你要用 CAP 给这套系统定一条非功能需求。
scenario_en: Twitter runs across data centers so partitions will happen, and you want to state one CAP-based non-functional requirement.
q: 用 CAP 定非功能需求时，正确的问法是？
options: 「优先一致性还是可用性？」（P 是前提）
「要 C、A、P 里的哪两个？」三选二随便选
「能不能三个都要？」
CAP 与非功能需求无关
options_en: "Consistency or availability?" (P is already a given).
"Which two of C, A, P do we want?" — just pick any two.
"Can we have all three?"
CAP has nothing to do with non-functional requirements.
why: 分布式系统必须容忍分区，所以 P 不是选项而是前提；真正要回答的是这套系统更看重一致性还是可用性。
why_en: Partition tolerance is a given in distributed systems, so the real CAP question is whether to prioritize consistency or availability.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P["Partition is given"] --> Q{"Need newest data?"}
    Q -->|Yes| C["Prefer consistency"]
    Q -->|No| A["Prefer availability"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统在网络分区下只能同时保证一致性与可用性中的一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In a network partition a distributed system can guarantee only consistency or availability, not both.

q_en: What is the right CAP question when defining non-functional requirements?
optionExplanations: 对，分区容错是分布式系统的前提，真正要答的是一致性还是可用性优先。
任选两个掩盖了分区容错根本不能放弃这个事实。
网络分区一旦发生，就必须在一致性和可用性间二选一，不能三者兼得。
CAP 直接决定该选哪种一致性模型，怎么会跟需求无关。
optionExplanations_en: Right — partition tolerance is a given in distributed systems; the real choice is consistency or availability.
'Pick any two' hides the fact that partition tolerance can never actually be dropped.
Once a partition happens you must choose between consistency and availability, not keep all three.
CAP directly shapes which consistency model you pick, so it's far from irrelevant to requirements.

scenario: Twitter 日常流量平稳，但世界杯决赛当晚推文量暴涨；扩展性这条 NFR 要写出信息量。
scenario_en: Twitter traffic is steady most days but explodes during a World Cup final, and your scalability requirement has to say something useful.
q: 评估「扩展性」这条非功能需求时，除了总量还要特别考虑什么？
options: 机房该建在哪个国家或城市的物理位置
编程语言本身的运行时性能
服务器硬件的品牌与型号
突发流量（高峰/节假日）以及读写比
options_en: Which country or city to physically locate the data center in.
The programming language's runtime performance.
The server hardware brand and model.
Bursty traffic (peak hours or holidays) and the read/write ratio.
why: 所有系统都要扩展，值得写进 NFR 的是「独特的扩展需求」：某时段的 bursty 流量、大事件洪峰、以及读写比例。
why_en: For scalability, consider unique needs like bursty traffic at certain times, event spikes, and whether reads or writes need to scale more.
q_en: When evaluating scalability as an NFR, what should you consider besides total volume?
optionExplanations: 机房选址属于基础设施决策，不是需求环节该回答的问题。
语言运行时性能是实现细节，不是架构层面的扩展性。
服务器品牌不会改变要不要分片、要不要读写分离的判断。
对，突发流量和读写比才是扩展性里真正有信息量的部分。
optionExplanations_en: Site selection is an infrastructure decision, not something requirements gathering answers.
Runtime performance is an implementation detail, not architecture-level scalability.
Hardware brand doesn't change whether you need sharding or read replicas.
Right — bursty traffic and the read/write ratio are the informative part of scalability.

scenario: 同一套框架下要分别给社交动态和银行流水写持久性 NFR，两者丢一条数据的代价差得很远。
scenario_en: You write a durability requirement for a social feed and for bank transactions, where the cost of losing one record is wildly different.
q: 「持久性」要求因业务而异，教科书式的对比是？
options: 游戏内进度绝不能丢，而银行流水丢几笔可以接受
社交网络可容忍少量数据丢失，银行系统绝对不行
所有系统都不能丢任何一条数据
持久性只取决于磁盘型号
options_en: Game progress must never be lost, while losing a few bank ledger entries is acceptable.
A social network can tolerate some data loss; a banking system cannot.
No system can ever afford to lose a single record.
Durability depends only on the disk model.
why: 持久性该问『丢数据的代价有多大』：社交网络丢一条动态可以忍，银行丢一笔交易不可接受，这是延迟成本 vs 数据丢失成本的取舍。
why_en: A social network might tolerate some data loss, but a banking system cannot, which is the classic durability contrast.
tradeoff: 社交场景『容忍少量丢失换更简单/更快的写路径』 vs 金融场景『零丢失优先，接受更重的写路径』
q_en: What is the textbook contrast for durability requirements across businesses?
optionExplanations: 把顺序说反了：真正不能丢的是银行流水，游戏进度通常能接受重来。
对，社交动态丢一条能忍，银行交易丢一笔不行——这是丢数据代价的真实差异。
一刀切要求零丢失会让所有系统都背上不必要的强一致写入成本。
把持久性单一归因到磁盘型号，忽略了副本数和写确认策略才是真正杠杆。
optionExplanations_en: This flips it — bank ledgers are the side that must never be lost; game progress can usually be replayed.
Right — a lost social post is tolerable, a lost bank transaction isn't; that's the real cost gap.
Demanding zero loss everywhere saddles every system with needless strong-write overhead.
Pinning durability on disk model alone misses the real levers: replica count and write acks.

scenario: 非功能需求检查清单一共有 CAP、环境约束、扩展性、延迟、持久性、安全、容错、合规八项。
q: 从这八项检查清单里，最终应挑出几条与系统最相关的非功能需求？
options: 全部 8 条都写
只挑 1 条
10 条以上
options_en: Write down all eight.
Pick just one.
Three to five.
More than ten.
why: 识别与本系统最相关的 top 3-5 条 NFR；全写会稀释深挖环节的火力，只写一条又撑不起完整的品质画像。
why_en: Identify the three to five non-functional requirements most relevant to your system.
q_en: From the eight NFR checklist items, how many should you finally choose for the system?
scenario_en: The NFR checklist has eight items: CAP, environment constraints, scalability, latency, durability, security, fault tolerance, and compliance.
optionExplanations: 全部 8 条都写会稀释深挖环节，火力被摊得太薄。
只挑 1 条又撑不起完整的品质画像，覆盖不了关键风险。
对，3-5 条刚好覆盖与本系统最相关的品质，又留得住深挖时间。
10 条以上早就超出清单本身，等于没有做任何取舍。
optionExplanations_en: Writing all eight dilutes the deep-dive time you need to spend on each one.
Just one item is too thin to cover the system's real quality risks.
Right — three to five covers the qualities that matter most and still leaves deep-dive time.
Ten-plus overshoots the checklist itself, which means no real prioritization happened.

scenario: 面试开场刚定完需求。很多备考指南建议此时先做一轮 back-of-the-envelope 容量估算（存储、DAU、QPS）；而本课程（Hello Interview）的 delivery framework 对此持不同立场。
q: 本框架推荐的做法是？
options: 必须先算完存储、DAU、QPS 再动手设计
向面试官说明：跳过开场估算，需要时再算
让面试官替你把数字算出来
整场面试完全不做任何计算
options_en: Finish estimating storage, DAU, and QPS before doing anything else.
Tell the interviewer you'll skip upfront estimation and do the math only when needed.
Ask the interviewer to do the numbers for you.
Do no calculations at all during the whole interview.
why: 本课程的框架认为开场估算常常只得到「很大」，不改变任何设计决策；所以先跟面试官说明跳过，等某个数字真的会改变架构（比如要不要分片）时再当场算。
why_en: This course's framework holds that upfront estimates usually just conclude "it's big" and change no decisions, so tell the interviewer you'll skip them and do the math only when a number actually changes the architecture, such as whether to shard.
whenOtherWins: 当结果直接决定架构时必须算：比如 TopK 热门话题要估话题总数，才能决定 min-heap 用单实例还是要分片。
tradeoff: 开场就估算『看似严谨但常无信号』 vs 按需估算『省时间，只在改变设计时才算』
q_en: What does this framework recommend for early back-of-the-envelope estimates?
scenario_en: You have just finished requirements. Many prep guides suggest an upfront back-of-the-envelope pass on storage, DAU, and QPS here; the Hello Interview delivery framework used in this course takes a different stance.
optionExplanations: 面试一开场就先算完存储/DAU/QPS，常只得到很大，挤占后面的设计时间。
对，先跟考官说清楚：开场先不算，等某个数字真的会改架构再当场算。
把估算责任转嫁给考官，考官不会替你完成本该属于你的判断。
完全不算也会在遇到分片阈值这类真正需要数字的场景时卡住。
optionExplanations_en: Estimating storage, DAU, and QPS up front usually ends in 'it's a lot' and eats design time.
Right — tell the interviewer you'll skip the opener and estimate only when a number changes the design.
Shifting the estimate onto the interviewer skips a judgment call that's actually yours to make.
Never calculating at all will stall you later when a real sharding-threshold decision needs a number.

scenario: 45 分钟设计面，你花 6 分钟算出 500TB 存储和 10k QPS，然后说了句「嗯，很大」就翻页。
scenario_en: You spent six of your forty-five minutes deriving 500 terabytes and 10k QPS, said "so, it is big", and moved on.
q: 算了一通存储/DAU/QPS，结论只是「嗯，很大」，考官从中得到了什么信号？
options: 对系统规模的深刻理解
扩展性方面一个能落地的具体设计信号
对估算能力的认可
除了『你会基础算术』以外什么都没有
options_en: Deep insight into the system's scale.
A concrete, actionable design signal about scalability.
Credit for your estimation ability.
Nothing except proof that you can do basic arithmetic.
why: 不影响设计的估算是表演式计算；考官点明这种算术除了证明会加减乘除毫无信号。
why_en: Calculating storage and QPS just to conclude it is a lot gives the interviewer nothing except proof you can do arithmetic.
q_en: If your storage, DAU, and QPS math only concludes “it is large,” what signal does the interviewer get?
optionExplanations: 算出一个很大的数字不等于理解了系统，考官看不到具体判断。
任何估算天然指向具体架构选择是误解，没落到动作就没信号。
考官真正在意的是判断力，不是心算速度，这不是在考算术。
对，这类计算除了证明你会加减乘除，没给出任何设计信号。
optionExplanations_en: A big final number doesn't equal real system understanding — the interviewer sees no judgment behind it.
Assuming any estimate naturally points to a concrete choice is the misread; no action, no signal.
Interviewers care about judgment, not mental-math speed — this isn't an arithmetic test.
Right — this kind of math proves only that you can do arithmetic, nothing about design.

scenario: 你在设计一个 TopK 热门话题系统：需要在内存里维护『当前最热的 K 个话题』。
q: 什么时候当场估算才是「必要」的？
options: 话题总数决定要不要分片
每场面试开始时都必须先估算一次
只在结束时总结陈述用
面试官心情好的时候顺便算一下
options_en: When the topic count decides whether to shard.
At the very start of every interview, no matter the system.
Only as a closing summary at the end.
Whenever the interviewer happens to be in a good mood.
why: TopK 例子：话题总数决定单个数据结构实例是否装得下，直接改变架构——这类计算才值得当场做。
why_en: Estimation matters when it changes the design, like estimating topic counts in a top-k system to decide between a single min-heap and a sharded one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在候选集合里持续维护排名前 K 的元素的问题模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K is the problem of continuously tracking the highest-ranked K elements in a set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 堆顶始终是最小值的二叉堆，常用来维护当前的 K 个最大候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap is a binary heap whose root is always the smallest element, often used to track the current top-K candidates.

q_en: When is it actually necessary to estimate during the interview?
scenario_en: You are designing a TopK trending-topics system that keeps the current hottest K topics in memory.
optionExplanations: 对，话题总数一旦超过单机容量，就必须引入分片和聚合——这才值得当场算。
把估算当成每场面试固定要做的开场仪式，和具体设计脱节。
总结阶段才算，已经画完的设计不会因为这个数字反过来被修改。
触发条件系在考官心情上，这种估算在真实面试里根本不可控。
optionExplanations_en: Right — once topic count exceeds single-machine capacity you must shard, and that's worth stopping to calculate.
Treating estimation as a fixed opening ritual for every interview disconnects it from the actual design.
Calculating only at the summary stage can't retroactively change a design you already drew.
Tying the trigger to the interviewer's mood makes it uncontrollable and unrepeatable.

scenario: 45 分钟设计 Twitter，核心实体环节只有 ~2 分钟，后面还要留时间给 API 和高层设计。
scenario_en: The core entities step gets about two minutes in a 45-minute Twitter design, with the API and high-level design still ahead.
q: 「核心实体」环节（约 2 分钟）要做什么？
options: 写出完整的数据库 schema 与所有字段类型
先画出最终版架构图
列出核心实体清单（第一稿）
把建表 SQL 写完整
options_en: Write out the complete database schema with every column type.
Draw the final architecture diagram first.
List the core entities as a first draft.
Write the complete CREATE TABLE SQL.
why: 先用一个简短的 bulleted list 列核心实体：定义术语、理解核心数据，作为 API 与数据模型的地基。
why_en: Spend about two minutes listing the core entities your API will exchange and your system will persist, framed as a first draft.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Actors["Actors"] --> Nouns["Core nouns"]
    Nouns --> API["API resources"]
    API --> Data["First data model"]
q_en: What should you do in the roughly two-minute core entities stage?
optionExplanations: 两分钟根本写不完完整 schema，只会挤占后面 API 环节的时间。
顺序反了：没有实体和 API，架构图根本无从画起。
对，先列一份可迭代的核心实体第一稿，后面发现新字段随时补。
字段还没定案就写建表 SQL，大概率很快就要推倒重写。
optionExplanations_en: Two minutes can't finish a full schema, and it eats into the time the API step needs.
This reverses the order — without entities and an API there's nothing to draw an architecture from.
Right — sketch a first-draft entity list you can iterate on as new fields surface later.
Writing CREATE TABLE SQL before fields are settled usually gets rewritten anyway.

scenario: 核心实体只有 ~2 分钟，而高层设计还没画，很多字段要等请求路径清楚后才知道。
scenario_en: Core entities gets two minutes and the high-level design does not exist yet, so most fields are still unknown.
q: 为什么核心实体环节不直接写完整数据模型？
options: 因为数据模型本来就不重要，写不写都无所谓
因为『不知道不知道什么』，先小清单迭代
因为面试官从来不看数据模型
因为手写字段太耗时
options_en: Because the data model doesn't really matter, so it makes no difference whether you write it.
Because you don't know what you don't know; start small and iterate.
Because interviewers never look at the data model.
Because writing out fields by hand takes too long.
why: 过早锁死 schema 会被后面的发现推翻；等高层设计里清楚了每个请求改什么状态，再补各实体的关键字段。
why_en: You don't know what you don't know yet, so start with a small entity list and add fields once the high-level design clarifies what each request updates.
q_en: Why should the core entities stage not become a full data model?
optionExplanations: 把暂缓误解成不重要，其实深挖环节还要回头标注字段。
对，问题是不知道不知道什么：先给小清单，等高层设计澄清了再补。
很多考官恰恰通过数据模型考察建模能力，谈不上从不看。
把根本原因简化成打字速度，其实提前锁定的字段迟早会被推翻。
optionExplanations_en: Mistakes 'deferred' for 'unimportant' — deep dives still come back to annotate fields.
Right — you don't know what you don't know yet, so start small and add fields once the design clarifies them.
Many interviewers specifically probe modeling skill through the data model, so this overstates it.
Reducing the reason to typing speed misses that fields locked too early get overturned regardless.

scenario: 45 分钟设计 Twitter，核心实体环节 ~2 分钟，你要靠几个自问快速筛出该写的名词。
scenario_en: With two minutes for core entities in a Twitter design, you need a few quick self-questions to filter the nouns worth listing.
q: 识别核心实体时，值得自问的问题有哪些？（多选）
options: 系统里的参与者（actors）是谁？他们有重叠吗？
满足功能需求需要哪些名词/资源？
实体名字起得清晰吗？
实体将来要部署在哪个可用区？
options_en: Who are the actors in the system? Do they overlap?
What nouns or resources are needed to satisfy the functional requirements?
Are the entity names clear and well chosen?
Which availability zone will each entity be deployed to?
why: 找实体 = 找 actor + 找满足功能需求的名词；有的考官还会借命名质量观察你的基本功。部署位置不是这一步的事。
why_en: Ask who the actors are and which nouns are needed to satisfy the functional requirements, and choose good names for them.
q_en: Which questions are useful when identifying core entities? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 从谁在用系统倒推实体，重叠的 actor（如既发帖又关注）能省掉重复实体。
从功能需求正推需要的名词，直接把需求清单映射成实体清单。
命名模糊像 Data、Info 会被考官当成负面信号，清晰命名是基本功。
可用区属于部署阶段的决定，这时候讨论明显为时过早。
optionExplanations_en: Works backward from who uses the system; overlapping actors, like a poster who also follows, avoid duplicate entities.
Works forward from the requirements to the nouns they need, mapping straight onto an entity list.
Vague names like Data or Info read as a negative signal — clear naming is a basic skill being checked.
Availability zone is a deployment decision, far too early to raise at this step.

scenario: 45 分钟设计 Twitter，核心功能是发推、关注、看关注流，实体清单只能写 2 分钟。
scenario_en: The core features are posting, following and reading the feed, and you have two minutes to list entities.
q: Twitter 例子的核心实体清单是？
options: User、Tweet、Follow
Server、Database、Cache
Post、Comment、Like、Share、Ad、DM
只有 Tweet 一个实体
options_en: User, Tweet, Follow.
Server, Database, Cache.
Post, Comment, Like, Share, Ad, DM.
Just Tweet, and nothing else.
why: 三个实体就够撑起核心功能：User 发 Tweet、User 之间 Follow；组件（服务器/缓存）不是业务实体。
why_en: For Twitter the core entities are simply the user, the tweet, and the follow relationship.
q_en: What is the core entity list for the Twitter example?
optionExplanations: 对，三个业务名词刚好撑起发推、关注、看 feed 这三条核心线。
服务器、数据库、缓存是高层设计里的组件，不是业务实体。
把六种功能都当实体列出来，早就超出了两分钟该有的范围。
少了 Follow 就定义不出该展示谁的推文，feed 无从谈起。
optionExplanations_en: Right — three business nouns are enough to carry posting, following, and feed reads.
Server, database, and cache are high-level-design components, not business entities.
Listing six separate features as entities blows well past what a two-minute step should cover.
Without Follow there's no way to define whose tweets to show in the feed.

scenario: Twitter 的核心实体已列好，接下来 ~5 分钟要产出能让高层设计逐个搭建的东西。
scenario_en: Core entities are listed, and the next five minutes have to produce something the high-level design can be built against.
q: API / 系统接口环节的目的？
options: 向考官展示你会写代码
确定服务器数量
选择云厂商
定义系统与用户的契约
options_en: Show the interviewer that you can write code.
To determine how many servers you need.
To pick a cloud vendor.
To define the contract between the system and its users.
why: 先定契约再画架构：API 保证你的设计对得上需求，之后高层设计可以逐 endpoint 搭建。
why_en: The API defines the contract between your system and its users, usually mapping to the functional requirements and guiding the high-level design.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Req["Functional reqs"] --> API["API contract"]
    API --> HLD["High-level design"]
    HLD --> Deep["Deep dive"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统对外暴露的调用契约，规定客户端能发起哪些请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the contract a system exposes, defining which requests a client can make.

q_en: What is the purpose of the API or system interface stage?
optionExplanations: 写代码留给深挖里的伪代码/命令，不是这一步该展示的东西。
服务器数量属于容量估算或深挖，不是契约环节要决定的。
云厂商选择几乎不会出现在这套面试框架里。
对，先定好系统与用户之间的契约，才能指导后面的高层设计。
optionExplanations_en: Actual code belongs in deep-dive pseudocode or commands, not this step's job.
Server count belongs to capacity estimation or deep dives, not the contract step.
Vendor choice almost never shows up in this interview framework at all.
Right — settle the contract between system and users first; it then guides the high-level design.

scenario: 普通产品型系统设计面试，客户端形态单一，也没有特殊的服务间性能诉求，要快速选定 API 协议。
q: 默认应该选哪种 API 协议？
options: REST
GraphQL
gRPC
SOAP
options_en: REST.
GraphQL.
gRPC.
SOAP.
why: 别过度思考协议选择：没有特殊理由就默认 REST，它简单、通用、考官零解释成本。
why_en: Default to REST, which uses HTTP verbs for CRUD on resources, unless you have a specific reason not to.
whenOtherWins: 客户端多样、数据需求差异大 → GraphQL；内部服务间通信、性能关键 → RPC/gRPC；对接遗留企业系统 → SOAP。
tradeoff: REST『通用、零解释成本』 vs 专用协议『更贴合特定约束，但引入额外复杂度』

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 HTTP 动词对资源做增删改查的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that uses HTTP verbs to perform CRUD operations on resources.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端可以精确声明所需字段的查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language that lets the client specify exactly which fields it needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 开源的高性能 RPC 框架，常用于服务间通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's high-performance remote-procedure-call framework, often used for service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 XML 的老式企业级 Web 服务协议，报文冗长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOAP is an older XML-based enterprise web-service protocol with verbose messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对资源的四种基本操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRUD stands for the four basic operations: create, read, update, and delete.

q_en: Which API protocol should you choose by default?
scenario_en: You are designing a normal product interview system with one main client type and no special service-to-service performance constraint.
optionExplanations: 对，客户端单一又没有特殊诉求时默认选它，资源化加 HTTP 动词，考官零解释成本。
客户端字段需求差异很大时才划算，单一客户端下反而多背一层 schema。
内部服务间调用、追求极致性能时才该选，对外产品接口用不上这个优势。
只适合对接遗留企业系统，新系统默认选它会平白带来冗余复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: Right — default here since the client is simple and nothing special is needed: resource verbs, zero explanation cost.
Worth it only when client field needs vary a lot; with one client it just adds a schema layer.
Fits internal service-to-service calls chasing top performance, an edge this public API doesn't need.
Fits legacy enterprise integration only; defaulting to it here adds needless complexity.

scenario: 系统要同时服务移动端、网页端、手表端等多种客户端，各端需要的数据字段差异很大，担心接口返回太多或太少数据。
q: 最匹配的 API 风格是？
options: REST 固定返回全部字段
为每种客户端各复制一套 REST API
GraphQL——客户端精确声明要什么数据
改用 FTP 传输数据
options_en: REST that always returns every field.
Duplicate a separate REST API for each client type.
GraphQL — clients specify exactly what data they want.
Switch to FTP for data transfer.
why: GraphQL 让客户端按需取数，正好解决多样客户端 over-fetch/under-fetch 的痛点。
why_en: GraphQL lets each client specify exactly the data it needs, avoiding over-fetching and under-fetching across diverse clients.
whenOtherWins: 客户端单一、标准 CRUD 场景下 REST 更简单直接，不必引入 GraphQL 的额外复杂度。
tradeoff: GraphQL『按需取数，避免 over/under-fetch』 vs REST『固定形状，简单但可能取多或取少』

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 HTTP 动词对资源做增删改查的 API 风格，返回字段通常固定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style using HTTP verbs on resources, usually with a fixed response shape.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端可以精确声明所需字段的查询语言，避免多拿或少拿数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language letting clients specify exactly which fields they need, avoiding over- or under-fetching.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于批量传输文件的协议，不适合按字段取数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FTP is a protocol for bulk file transfer, not suited to field-level data fetching.

q_en: Which API style best fits this case?
scenario_en: The system serves mobile, web, and watch clients, and each client needs a different field shape from the API.
optionExplanations: 字段形状固定不变时才够用，多端差异大就会白白多传没人要的数据。
端数少且差异固定时能凑合，端一多接口数量线性膨胀，维护成本失控。
对，字段需求因端而异时选它，同一接口让每端自己声明要哪些字段。
只适合批量传文件，没有字段级查询能力，接不住这种结构化数据需求。
optionExplanations_en: Works when the field shape never changes; with diverse clients it wastes bandwidth on unused fields.
Tolerable with a few fixed clients; as client types grow, endpoints multiply into real maintenance debt.
Right — pick this when field needs differ by client: one endpoint, each client declares its own shape.
Fits bulk file transfer only; it has no field-level query ability for this structured-data need.

scenario: 设计内部微服务之间的调用接口：不对外暴露，追求最低开销与最高性能。
q: 最合适的协议是？
options: 把对外暴露的那套 REST 契约直接搬来复用
RPC，如 gRPC：动作导向，序列化更高效
GraphQL 按需查询协议
轮询加邮件通知机制
options_en: Reuse the same public-facing REST contract for internal calls.
RPC such as gRPC — action-oriented with efficient serialization.
GraphQL.
Polling plus email notifications.
why: RPC/gRPC 面向动作、序列化高效，在性能关键的内部 service-to-service 通信里快过 REST。
why_en: Use RPC like gRPC for internal service-to-service APIs where performance is critical, since it is faster than REST.
whenOtherWins: 面向外部用户/第三方的公开 API 应默认 REST——生态、可调试性和通用性更好。
tradeoff: gRPC『更快更省，但对外生态和可调试性弱』 vs REST『通用易调试，但内部调用开销更高』

termDefinitions.meaning: 像调用本地函数一样调用远程服务的动作型协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPC lets a client call a remote service like a local function, oriented around actions.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 开源的高性能 RPC 框架，用二进制协议序列化，常用于服务间通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's high-performance RPC framework that uses a binary protocol for serialization, often used between services.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 HTTP 动词对资源做增删改查的通用 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is a general-purpose API style using HTTP verbs on resources.

q_en: Which protocol best fits this internal service-to-service case?
scenario_en: You are designing internal microservice calls that are not public and care most about low overhead and high performance.
optionExplanations: 对外契约拿来对内复用时，文本序列化和资源语义反而成了多余开销。
对，服务间调用追求低开销和高性能时选它，动作导向、二进制序列化更快更省。
解决的是客户端字段差异，不是内部调用的性能瓶颈，这里用不上。
延迟是秒级到分钟级，远远够不上性能关键这个约束。
optionExplanations_en: Reusing the external contract internally turns REST's text serialization into wasted overhead.
Right — pick this for low-overhead, high-performance service calls: action-oriented, binary serialization.
This solves client field diversity, not internal call performance — the wrong lever here.
Its latency runs seconds to minutes, nowhere near what 'performance-critical' requires.

scenario: 要设计的系统带实时通知，API 环节只有 ~5 分钟，实时通道选型很容易吃掉整段时间。
scenario_en: The system needs real-time notifications, the API step has five minutes, and picking a real-time transport can eat all of it.
q: 系统有实时功能（如实时通知）时，API 环节的正确处理是？
options: 把所有接口都改成 WebSocket
认为实时功能无法在这套框架里实现
先设计核心 API，实时功能后补
用轮询代替所有接口
options_en: Convert every endpoint to WebSocket.
Conclude real-time features can't be built in this framework.
Design the core API first; add real-time support later.
Replace every endpoint with polling.
why: 实时特性最终要靠 WebSocket/SSE，但别让它打乱节奏：先定核心 API，再在深挖里处理实时通道。
why_en: For real-time features you will need WebSockets or server-sent events, but design your core API first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持全双工、长连接的通信协议，适合双向实时推送。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a full-duplex, persistent-connection protocol suited to real-time bidirectional updates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器单向持续推送事件给客户端的轻量协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Server-sent events let a server continuously push updates to a client over one connection.

q_en: How should you handle real-time features, such as notifications, during the API stage?
optionExplanations: 把实时需求泛化到每个接口，大多数 CRUD 根本不需要长连接。
误以为这套框架处理不了实时功能，其实它有明确落点，深挖阶段。
对，核心 CRUD 先走 REST 定下来，实时推送留到深挖再开专用通道。
轮询延迟高、请求量大，替代不了真正的实时推送。
optionExplanations_en: Generalizing the real-time need to every endpoint forces long connections most CRUD calls don't need.
Wrongly assumes this framework can't handle real time — it actually has a clear home in deep dives.
Right — settle core CRUD on REST first, then add a dedicated real-time channel during deep dives.
Polling has high latency and request volume; it can't substitute for real push.

scenario: 按 REST 惯例为 Twitter 设计「发推」接口，当前用户由请求头里的认证 token 识别。
q: 哪个 endpoint 设计最符合惯例？
options: POST /v1/tweets，body 只带 { "text": string }
POST /v1/tweet?user_id=123&text=hello
GET /v1/createTweet
POST /v1/tweets，body 带 { "user_id": string, "text": string }
options_en: POST /v1/tweets with a body containing only { "text": string }.
POST /v1/tweet?user_id=123&text=hello.
GET /v1/createTweet.
POST /v1/tweets with a body containing { "user_id": string, "text": string }.
why: 资源用复数名词（tweets）、创建用 POST、正文只带业务数据；当前用户从 auth token 推导，绝不由客户端在 body 里自报。
why_en: Use a plural resource name with POST and put only the tweet text in the body, deriving the current user from the auth token.
whenOtherWins: 内部高性能调用可用 gRPC 的动作型接口，那时不必套 REST 资源惯例。
tradeoff: 从 token 推导身份『多一次校验，但杜绝伪造』 vs 由客户端传参『少一步，但任何人可冒充他人』
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
    C["Client"] -->|POST /v1/tweets| S["Server"]
    S --> A["user from token"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 HTTP 动词对资源做增删改查的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style using HTTP verbs to perform CRUD on resources.

termDefinitions.meaning: 认证后颁发的凭证，服务端用它推导当前用户身份，而非信任客户端参数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An auth token is issued after authentication, and the server uses it to derive the current user instead of trusting client-supplied parameters.

q_en: Which endpoint design best follows REST conventions?
scenario_en: Design the Twitter create-tweet endpoint using REST conventions; the current user comes from the auth token in the request headers.
optionExplanations: 对，资源名用复数、正文只放业务字段，服务端凭认证凭证识别当前用户，不可伪造。
user_id 混进查询字符串，任何人改一下参数就能冒充别人发推。
GET 语义上是只读，用它承载会改变状态的创建动作，还可能被缓存或预取。
身份既然要从 token 重新校验，客户端在正文里自报就是多余且危险的一步。
optionExplanations_en: Right — plural resource name, body holds only business data, and the server reads identity off the credential instead of trusting the client.
user_id rides in the query string, so anyone can edit the parameter and post as someone else.
GET is semantically read-only for a state-changing create action, and it risks caching or prefetch.
If the server must re-verify identity from the token anyway, letting the client self-report it is pointless and risky.

scenario: 发推接口把当前用户写在请求体的 user_id 字段里，服务端直接读取这个字段当作作者。
q: 让客户端在请求体里传 user_id 来标识「当前用户」，隐患是什么？
options: 请求体会变大，浪费带宽
JSON 解析速度变慢
接口无法做 HTTP 缓存
任何人都能伪造别人的身份发帖
options_en: The request body gets larger, wasting bandwidth.
JSON parsing becomes slower.
The endpoint can no longer use HTTP caching.
Anyone can forge another user's identity and post as them.
why: 身份来自认证而非输入：始终从 auth token 推导当前用户，否则请求体里的 user_id 可被随意篡改冒充。
why_en: Never take the current user's identity from the request body; derive it from the authentication token, or anyone can impersonate anyone.
codeSample:
# 不安全：身份来自可篡改的请求体
POST /v1/tweets
body: { "user_id": "123", "text": "hi" }

# 安全：身份来自认证 token
POST /v1/tweets
Authorization: Bearer <token>
body: { "text": "hi" }   # user 从 token 解出

termDefinitions.meaning: 认证后颁发的凭证，服务端应从它推导当前用户，而不是信任请求体字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An auth token is issued after authentication, and the server should derive the current user from it rather than trusting a body field.

q_en: What is the risk of letting the client send user_id as the current user?
scenario_en: The create-tweet endpoint reads user_id from the request body and treats that value as the post author.
optionExplanations: 多一个 user_id 字段带来的带宽开销小到可以忽略，不是真正的隐患。
多解析一个短字符串字段构不成性能瓶颈，问题不在这里。
POST 创建类接口本来就很少依赖 HTTP 缓存，这不是它的风险点。
对，攻击者只需改一个字段就能以他人身份发帖，身份必须从 token 推导。
optionExplanations_en: The bandwidth from one extra user_id field is negligible, not the actual risk here.
Parsing one more short string field isn't a performance bottleneck; that's not the issue.
POST create endpoints rarely rely on HTTP caching anyway, so that's not the exposure.
Right — an attacker only has to edit one field to post as someone else; identity must come from the token.

scenario: API 环节 ~5 分钟，你要为 Twitter 的发推和读流写出 HTTP 路径，考官看的是 REST 惯例。
scenario_en: You have five minutes to write HTTP paths for posting and reading tweets, and the interviewer is watching for REST conventions.
q: REST 资源命名的惯例是？
options: 复数名词（/tweets 而不是 /tweet）
动词短语路径（/createTweet 这类）
全大写路径（/TWEETS）
命名随意，怎么写都行
options_en: Plural nouns, like /tweets instead of /tweet.
Verb phrases, like /createTweet.
All-uppercase paths, like /TWEETS.
Naming doesn't matter — anything goes.
why: REST 把系统建模成资源集合：路径用复数名词表示事物集合，动作交给 HTTP 动词表达。
why_en: REST resources are plural nouns representing things in your system, with actions expressed by HTTP verbs.
codeSample:
GET  /v1/tweets        # list
GET  /v1/tweets/{id}   # read one
POST /v1/tweets        # create (verb is the HTTP method, not the path)
q_en: What is the REST convention for naming resources?
optionExplanations: 对，路径命名事物集合用复数名词，动作交给 GET/POST 这些 HTTP 方法表达。
把动作硬编码进路径，动词一多端点就会膨胀成一堆不一致的接口。
大小写只是排版风格，不是 REST 惯例真正关心的维度。
放弃一致性会让团队协作时接口风格因人而异、难以预测。
optionExplanations_en: Right — paths name a collection with a plural noun; actions are expressed through the HTTP method instead.
Hardcoding an action into the path breeds a sprawling set of inconsistent endpoints as verbs multiply.
Casing is just formatting style, not a dimension REST convention actually cares about.
Abandoning consistency leaves every teammate's endpoints styled differently and hard to predict.

scenario: 你在设计网页爬虫：系统本质是对输入执行一长串处理步骤、产出结果的数据处理系统。
q: API 之后、高层设计之前，可选做的一步是？
options: 直接开始容量估算
用简单列表描述数据流
先写单元测试
先画完整 ER 图
options_en: Jump straight into capacity estimation.
List the data flow as a simple sequence of actions.
Write unit tests first.
Draw the complete ER diagram first.
why: 数据处理型系统值得先列数据流（约 5 分钟），它会直接支撑接下来的高层设计。
why_en: For data-processing systems, optionally spend five minutes listing the high-level sequence of actions the system performs.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统没有长动作序列（普通 CRUD 产品），直接跳过数据流环节，进入高层设计。
tradeoff: 先列数据流『多花 5 分钟，换高层设计更顺』 vs 跳过它『省时间，仅适合无长处理链的系统』

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述实体及其相互关系的图示，通常在数据模型定案后画。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ER diagram shows entities and their relationships, usually drawn once the data model is settled.

q_en: What optional step can come after APIs and before high-level design?
scenario_en: You are designing a web crawler, a data-processing system that applies a sequence of steps to input and produces output.
optionExplanations: 只有数字会马上改变组件选择时才该在这里插估算，多数场景没到这一步。
对，爬虫、ETL 这类处理链系统值得先列一份高层动作清单，直接支撑后面的设计。
接口和架构都还没定，此时写单元测试根本没有代码可测。
字段关系还会随高层设计调整，这时候画完整 ER 图大概率要推倒重来。
optionExplanations_en: Estimating here only makes sense when a number would immediately flip the component choice, rarely the case yet.
Right — crawlers and ETL pipelines benefit from a high-level action list first; it directly drives the design.
Neither the API nor the architecture exists yet, so there's nothing for a unit test to target.
Field relationships will still shift with high-level design, so a full ER diagram here usually gets redrawn.

q: 把网页爬虫的数据流排成正确顺序：
why: 爬虫数据流：取种子 URL → 解析 HTML → 提取 URL → 存数据 → 重复。这份清单直接指导高层设计。
why_en: A web crawler fetches seed URLs, parses the HTML, extracts new URLs, stores the data, and repeats.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Seed["Seed URL"] --> Fetch["Fetch HTML"]
    Fetch --> Parse["Parse"]
    Parse --> Links["Extract links"]
    Links --> Store["Store data"]
    Store --> Seed
q_en: Put the web crawler data flow in the correct order:

scenario: 45 分钟设计 Twitter，API 契约已定，接下来 10-15 分钟是白板上产出最多的一段。
scenario_en: The API contract is set, and the next ten to fifteen minutes are the highest-output stretch on the board.
q: 高层设计（~10-15 分钟）环节的核心产出是？
options: 可运行的代码
一份完整的成本预算表
框和箭头：组件及其交互
详细的部署脚本
options_en: Runnable code.
A complete cost budget table.
Boxes and arrows for components and their interactions.
Detailed deployment scripts.
why: 高层设计就是画组件图：首要目标是支撑住已设计的 API——满足了 API 也就满足了需求。
why_en: High-level design means drawing boxes and arrows for components like servers, databases, and caches to satisfy the API you defined.
q_en: What is the core output of the high-level design stage?
optionExplanations: 写代码属于实现阶段，不属于这套框架任何一个计时环节。
成本预算几乎不出现在系统设计面试的评分点里。
对，组件图直接回答每个 API 请求怎样被满足，这才是这一步的产出。
部署脚本细到实现层，远超出这 10-15 分钟该有的颗粒度。
optionExplanations_en: Writing code belongs to implementation, not any timed step in this framework.
Cost budgeting almost never shows up as a scoring point in these interviews.
Right — the component diagram directly answers how each API request gets satisfied, the real output here.
Deployment scripts go down to implementation detail, well past this ten-to-fifteen-minute step's scope.

scenario: 设计 Twitter 这类请求驱动的产品系统，上一步已经列好了 API endpoint。进入高层设计，面对空白画布，担心漏掉需求。
q: 最稳的推进方式是？
options: 先把所有可能会用上的组件一次性全摆上画布
从数据库开始，向外逐步补充
先画好全球多机房容灾方案
逐个过 API endpoint 搭建组件
options_en: Put every component you might conceivably need on the canvas all at once first.
Start from the database and build outward.
Draw a global multi-region disaster-recovery setup first.
Go through API endpoints one by one, building components.
why: API 已经列好，每个 endpoint 对应一条功能需求；逐个过 endpoint、它需要什么组件就补什么，画完所有 endpoint 也就覆盖了所有需求。数据管道类系统（如爬虫）则更适合按 data flow 推进。
why_en: With the API already listed, each endpoint maps to a functional requirement; walking them one by one and adding what each needs means the finished diagram covers every requirement. Data-pipeline systems like crawlers fit a data-flow walk better.
whenOtherWins: 数据处理型系统（如爬虫）按 data flow 的步骤顺序推进更自然，而不是按 endpoint。
tradeoff: 逐 endpoint 搭建『天然贴合需求，但节奏依赖 API 清晰度』 vs 一次性堆全部组件『看似全面，实际容易偏离需求』
q_en: What is the safest way to move through high-level design?
scenario_en: You are designing a request-driven product system like Twitter and have already listed the API endpoints. Now you face a blank canvas in high-level design and want a path that does not miss requirements.
optionExplanations: 一开始就想着全覆盖，多数组件到最后根本用不上，等于白画。
存储是核心难点的题才该这样起手，多数场景会先陷进表结构、丢了请求路径。
多机房容灾是深挖阶段的加固内容，这时候引入会拖慢高层设计的节奏。
对，逐个过 API endpoint 搭组件，每加一个都对应一条需求，不容易跑偏。
optionExplanations_en: Trying to cover everything up front leaves many components unused — wasted drawing time.
This fits storage-centric problems; most cases get stuck in table detail and lose the request path.
Multi-region resilience is deep-dive hardening; pulling it forward here just stalls the pace.
Right — walk endpoints one by one and build what each needs; every piece maps to a requirement.

scenario: 高层设计只有 10-15 分钟，你在第 3 分钟就开始画缓存、消息队列和分片方案。
scenario_en: High-level design has ten to fifteen minutes and you start drawing caches, queues and sharding three minutes in.
q: 高层设计阶段过早堆复杂度（缓存、队列全上）最常见的下场是？
options: 复杂度提前耗掉时间，很可能来不及做完一个跑通主路径的完整方案
设计显得更完善，考官通常会给加分
反而节省了深挖环节的时间
面试官会主动替你简化设计
options_en: Complexity eats the clock early, so you likely run out of time before finishing a complete, working main path.
The design looks more thorough, so the interviewer usually adds points.
It actually saves time in the deep-dives step.
The interviewer will step in and simplify the design for you.
why: 这是极常见的失败：复杂度上得太早，时间被耗掉，往往来不及做完一个能跑通的方案。正确做法是发现可优化点时口头点一句、写个便签，继续推进主路径。
why_en: A very common failure: adding complexity too early burns the clock, and candidates often fail to finish a working design. Call out improvements briefly, note them, and keep building the main path.
q_en: What usually happens when you add caches, queues, and other complexity too early?
optionExplanations: 对，复杂度上得太早会先耗光时间，往往来不及把方案做完整。
堆砌组件本身不是加分项，考官更在意先满足核心功能。
深挖环节仍要单独花时间逐条对照非功能需求，提前处理省不掉它。
考官通常只提问和观察，不会主动替你把设计简化下来。
optionExplanations_en: Right — piling on complexity too early burns the clock, so you often run out of time before the design is complete.
Stacking components isn't itself a bonus; interviewers care more about meeting core functionality first.
Deep dives still need their own time against each NFR; doing it early doesn't buy that time back.
Interviewers mostly observe and probe — they won't step in and simplify the design for you.

scenario: 高层设计时考官全程在旁观察，你只闷头画框和箭头，他无法判断你是否懂请求路径。
scenario_en: The interviewer watches you draw boxes and arrows in silence and cannot tell whether you understand the request path.
q: 画高层设计时，嘴上应该同步讲什么？
options: 逐一报出每个组件的品牌和具体型号
数据怎样流经系统、每步状态如何变
背诵每个组件的发布年份
保持安静，专心画图就好
options_en: Call out each component's brand and specific model number one by one.
How data flows through the system: what state changes at each step.
Recite the release year of each component.
Stay silent and just focus on drawing.
why: 边画边讲思路：显式说明请求路径上的数据流与状态变更，请求到达持久层时顺手在库旁标注关键字段。
why_en: Talk through how data flows through the system and what state changes with each request, from the API call to the response.
q_en: What should you explain out loud while drawing the high-level design?
optionExplanations: 品牌型号对判断架构是否正确没有任何帮助。
对，讲清数据怎么流经系统、每一步状态怎么变，考官才能跟上你的判断。
发布年份是无关信息，不会影响任何设计判断。
全程沉默让考官只能看图猜测，评估不到你的思路。
optionExplanations_en: Brand and model do nothing to help judge whether the architecture is correct.
Right — narrate how data flows and what state changes at each step so the interviewer follows your reasoning.
Release year is irrelevant trivia with no bearing on any design decision.
Staying silent leaves the interviewer guessing from the diagram alone, with no way to assess your thinking.

scenario: 高层设计时间很紧，图上要给数据库标字段，而深挖阶段还可能推翻部分 schema。
scenario_en: Time is tight in high-level design, you are annotating the database on the diagram, and deep dives may still change the schema.
q: 在图上给数据库标注 schema 时，正确的详略度是？
options: 把每个表的所有列都写全，并逐一标注类型
完全不写任何字段
只记录与设计特别相关的列，类型也不用标
只写主键，其余全部省略
options_en: Write out every column of every table in full, and annotate each with its type.
Write no fields at all.
Note only the columns relevant to your design, and skip types.
Write only the primary key and omit everything else.
why: 别浪费时间抄显而易见的 schema；把字段写在数据库组件旁边、只写设计相关的，方便随设计演进而更新。
why_en: Document only the columns that matter to your design next to the database, skipping obvious fields and types the interviewer can infer.
q_en: How much schema detail should you write next to the database in the diagram?
optionExplanations: 把这两分钟的草稿环节当成完整建表任务，会占掉大量画图时间。
把信息量直接清零，深挖时想引用某个字段却发现图上根本没记录。
对，只写和设计相关的字段，考官一眼看到重点，还方便随设计更新。
压缩到只剩主键，反而把分片键、索引字段这些关键信息漏掉了。
optionExplanations_en: Treating this two-minute sketch as a full table definition eats up drawing time for nothing.
Zeroing out the detail means you'll want a field during deep dives and find it was never recorded.
Right — note only fields relevant to the design; interviewers see what matters and it stays easy to update.
Trimming down to just the primary key drops key fields like a shard key or index column too.

scenario: 远程面试用共享白板软件，45 分钟每分钟都在计时，而你从没用过这个工具。
scenario_en: It is a remote interview on a shared whiteboard tool, the clock runs the whole 45 minutes, and you have never used the tool.
q: 关于面试用的白板软件（如 Excalidraw），建议是？
options: 提前问招聘协调人用什么软件，并预先练熟
现场再摸索学习就行
坚持要求改用纸笔
用什么软件根本不重要，事先完全无需准备
options_en: Ask your recruiting coordinator ahead of time which tool you'll use, and practice it.
Figure it out live during the interview.
Insist on switching to pen and paper instead.
Which software you use doesn't matter at all, so there's no need to prepare in advance.
why: 别把宝贵时间浪费在跟工具搏斗上：提前向招聘协调人确认软件并练习到顺手。
why_en: Ask your recruiter which whiteboarding software you'll use and practice with it ahead of time so you're not fumbling in the interview.
q_en: What should you do about interview whiteboard tools like Excalidraw?
optionExplanations: 对，提前问清用什么软件并练熟，画图动作就不会占用设计思考的带宽。
现场摸索快捷键会挤占本该用于设计的分钟数。
多数公司面试流程固定，临时要求换工具通常不被允许。
工具生疏会拖慢画图节奏，这部分时间照样算进你的 45 分钟。
optionExplanations_en: Right — ask which tool ahead of time and practice it so drawing never competes with design thinking.
Fumbling for shortcuts live eats into minutes that should go toward the actual design.
Most companies run a fixed process; insisting on a swap usually isn't allowed.
Being unfamiliar with the tool slows your drawing, and that time still counts against your forty-five minutes.

scenario: 高层设计已画完，还剩 ~10 分钟，NFR 里的低延迟和高可用都还没被验证过。
scenario_en: The high-level design is drawn, about ten minutes remain, and none of your latency or availability requirements have been checked.
q: 深挖（Deep Dives）环节要用剩余 ~10 分钟做哪些事？（多选）
options: 确保设计满足所有非功能需求
处理边界情况、识别并解决瓶颈
根据面试官的追问改进设计
推翻高层设计重画一遍
options_en: Make sure the design meets every non-functional requirement.
Handle edge cases and identify and fix bottlenecks.
Improve the design based on the interviewer's probing questions.
Scrap the high-level design and redraw it from scratch.
why: 深挖 = 加固既有设计：对照 NFR 逐条满足、补边界、消瓶颈、回应探询——不是推倒重来。
why_en: Deep dives harden the design by meeting the non-functional requirements, addressing edge cases and bottlenecks, and improving based on interviewer probes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    NFR["NFRs"] --> Bottleneck["Bottlenecks"]
    Bottleneck --> Edge["Edge cases"]
    Edge --> Improve["Improve design"]
    Improve --> Signals["Answer probes"]
q_en: What should you do with the remaining roughly ten minutes for deep dives? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 把每条非功能需求都变成一段针对性讨论，没讨论到的等于没验收。
找出高层设计里扛不住压力或没覆盖到的边界，解决瓶颈才算真满足扩展性。
顺着考官的追问改进设计，精准命中他们想看的信号。
把深挖误当成重新设计的机会，会让已经验证过的高层设计前功尽弃。
optionExplanations_en: Turns each NFR into a targeted discussion — one left undiscussed is effectively unverified.
Finds where the high-level design can't take load; fixing bottlenecks is what actually satisfies scalability.
Follows the interviewer's probes to improve the design, precisely hitting the signal they're after.
Mistakes deep dives for a chance to redesign, wasting a high-level design already validated.

scenario: 同一道 Twitter 题面 senior 岗，深挖环节考官只丢了一句「还有什么想聊的吗？」
scenario_en: Same Twitter question but for a senior role, and at deep-dive time the interviewer just asks whether there is anything else you want to discuss.
q: 深挖环节里，junior 与 senior 候选人的差异是？
options: junior 必须自始至终比 senior 讲得更多
senior 可以直接跳过深挖环节
两者的主动性要求完全一样
junior 靠考官引导，senior 主动带节奏
options_en: Junior candidates must talk more than senior ones from start to finish.
Senior candidates can skip the deep-dives step entirely.
Both levels are expected to show identical proactivity.
Juniors lean on interviewer guidance; seniors lead proactively.
why: 主动性与级别成正比：越资深越要自己发现问题、带节奏，而不是等考官喂点。
why_en: Junior candidates can expect the interviewer to point out weak spots, while senior candidates should identify them and lead the deep dives themselves.
tradeoff: junior『被动应答，考官引导』 vs senior『主动识别薄弱点，自己带节奏』
q_en: How do junior and senior candidates differ in the deep-dive stage?
optionExplanations: 把差异归结成说话总量，考官不是按发言多少判断资深度的。
把资深误解成可以豁免这一环节，跳过深挖等于非功能需求全没验收。
忽略了主动性这个真正的区分维度，考官对不同级别的期待其实是分级的。
对，junior 靠考官引导发现薄弱点，senior 该自己主动带节奏、提出取舍。
optionExplanations_en: Reduces the gap to talk volume; interviewers don't judge seniority by how much you say.
Misreads seniority as an exemption — skipping deep dives leaves every NFR unverified.
Ignores proactivity, the real differentiator; interviewers actually scale expectations by level.
Right — juniors lean on interviewer guidance while seniors should surface issues and lead themselves.

scenario: 深挖只剩 10 分钟，考官带着一份想追问的信号清单，你却一口气讲了 8 分钟。
scenario_en: Ten minutes of deep dives left, the interviewer has a list of signals to probe, and you talk for eight of them straight.
q: 深挖环节滔滔不绝、盖住面试官说话的代价是？
options: 显得更主动，通常会加分
错过考官想收集的信号，拉低沟通分
对最终评估结果完全没有任何影响
可以借机多讲一个备选方案
options_en: It looks proactive and usually earns bonus points.
You miss the specific signals the interviewer wants and hurt your communication score.
It has no effect at all on the final evaluation outcome.
It's a chance to squeeze in one more alternative design.
why: 考官往往带着特定信号清单来提问；你说个不停就把机会说没了。主动和留白要平衡。
why_en: Talking over your interviewer makes you miss the specific signals they need and hurts your communication and collaboration evaluation.
q_en: What is the cost of talking nonstop and covering the interviewer during deep dives?
optionExplanations: 把说得多直接等同于主动，其实考官更看重能不能留出提问空间。
对，考官带着明确的信号清单来提问，插不上话就拿不到那部分分数。
沟通协作是明确写进评分项的独立维度，发言量当然会影响它。
备选方案挤占的正是考官原本想深挖的问题时间，不是加分项。
optionExplanations_en: Equates talking a lot with being proactive; interviewers actually value room to ask more.
Right — interviewers carry a specific signal checklist; no room to probe means missed points.
Communication is its own scored dimension, so talk volume absolutely affects it.
The extra alternative crowds out exactly the time the interviewer wanted to probe, not a bonus.

scenario: Twitter 有 100M+ DAU、feed 要求 <500ms 返回，深挖只剩 10 分钟，只够挖一个问题。
scenario_en: Twitter has over a hundred million daily actives and the feed must return in under 500 ms, and you have ten minutes for one deep dive.
q: Twitter 例子中，深挖环节「最有趣的问题」是？
options: 用户的注册与登录流程该怎么设计
推文的字数校验规则
低延迟 feed 的读写扩散取舍
机房该选址在哪里
options_en: How to design the user registration and login flow.
The tweet character-count validation rule.
Low-latency feed: fanout-on-read vs fanout-on-write.
Where to locate the data center.
why: 100M+ DAU 引出水平扩展/缓存/分片，而低延迟 feed 才是 Twitter 最有意思的深挖：读扩散 vs 写扩散加缓存。
why_en: For Twitter the most interesting deep dive is low-latency feed fetching, discussing fanout-on-read versus fanout-on-write plus caching.
tradeoff: fanout-on-write『写时推送，读取快但发帖贵』 vs fanout-on-read『读时聚合，写入便宜但大 V 读取慢』
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Feed["Low-latency feed"] --> Read["Fanout on read"]
    Feed --> Write["Fanout on write"]
    Read --> Cache["Cache hot reads"]
    Write --> Queue["Async fanout"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 读时才聚合所有关注对象的内容，写入便宜、读取慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout-on-read aggregates followed users' content at read time, keeping writes cheap but reads slower.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布时就把内容推送进每个粉丝的收件箱，读取快、写入更贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout-on-write pushes content into every follower's inbox at post time, making reads fast but writes more expensive.

q_en: In the Twitter example, what is the most interesting deep-dive problem?
optionExplanations: 注册流程是次要的账户功能，和低延迟 feed 这条非功能需求关系不大。
字数校验是一行代码能搞定的边界检查，没什么架构含量。
对，低延迟 feed（读扩散 vs 写扩散）才是撑住上亿日活最有意思的深挖。
机房选址是运维/合规话题，不是这道题该深挖的架构取舍。
optionExplanations_en: Registration is a minor account feature with little tie to the low-latency-feed NFR.
Character-count validation is a one-line boundary check with no architectural weight.
Right — low-latency feed (fanout-on-read vs on-write) is the interesting deep dive behind huge DAU.
Data-center siting is an ops/compliance topic, not the architectural trade-off this problem probes.

q: 补全深挖环节的四件事：
text: 深挖时：确保满足{{非功能需求}}、处理{{边界情况}}、识别并解决{{瓶颈}}、根据面试官的{{探询}}改进设计。
why: 这四件事就是『加固设计』的定义；每条非功能需求都应能对应到一段深挖讨论，而不是被口头带过。
why_en: Deep dives ensure the non-functional requirements are met, edge cases are handled, bottlenecks are fixed, and the design improves from interviewer probes.
q_en: Fill in the four jobs of the deep-dive stage:

scenario: 高层设计只剩 10 分钟，你边画主路径边冒出想法：这里加个缓存会更快、那里该挂个消息队列。
scenario_en: With 10 minutes left in the high-level design, while drawing the main path you keep spotting ideas — a cache here, a message queue there.
q: 发现这些可优化点时，正确动作是？
q_en: When you spot these optimizations, what's the right move?
options: 立刻停下，把缓存、消息队列、分片方案都画进去，先做出一版尽善尽美的架构
口头点一句、写个便签标记，继续把主路径画完，留到深挖再展开
记在脑子里就行，不必说也不必写，免得打断画图节奏
先跳过主路径，直接去深挖这几个优化点
options_en: Stop now and draw in the cache, the message queue, and sharding to make one perfect architecture.
Give a quick verbal callout plus a written note, finish the main path, and expand it in deep dives.
Just keep it in your head — no need to say or write it, so you keep your drawing rhythm.
Skip the main path and go deep-dive these optimizations right away.
why: 高层设计的目标是先搭出跑通主路径的简单骨架；优化点只做口头加便签的轻量标记，避免复杂度提前耗光时间。代价：便签上的每个点都要在深挖环节兑现，不能只喊不做。
why_en: Flag optimizations with a quick verbal callout plus a written note, then keep building the main path — premature complexity is why candidates never finish a working system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把热点数据放在快速存储里，减少对慢速数据库的读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache keeps hot data in fast storage to cut reads against the slower database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在生产者和消费者之间缓冲消息的中间件，用于异步解耦。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A message queue buffers messages between producers and consumers to decouple work asynchronously.

optionExplanations: 过早把缓存、队列、分片全画上，剩下的 10 分钟会被复杂度吃光，主路径反而跑不通。
对：轻量标记不打断主线，留到深挖兑现——高层设计要的是先跑通，不是先完美。
只记脑子里，深挖时容易忘，也让考官看不到你已识别出瓶颈，白丢主动性信号。
主路径还没通就去深挖，等于跳过了这一环节的唯一产出——一个满足需求的骨架。
optionExplanations_en: Drawing caches, queues, and sharding now burns the remaining 10 minutes, and the main path never runs end-to-end.
Right — a light marker doesn't derail the main line; deliver it in deep dives. High-level design aims for working, not perfect.
Keeping it only in your head risks forgetting in deep dives and hides from the interviewer that you spotted the bottleneck.
Deep-diving before the main path works skips this stage's only deliverable: a skeleton that meets the requirements.

scenario: 设计 Yelp：多数请求是简单读取，只有「按距离和评分搜附近餐厅」要跑真正的计算。你要写一条延迟 NFR。
scenario_en: Designing Yelp: most requests are simple reads; only 'search nearby restaurants by distance and rating' does real computation. You must write one latency NFR.
q: 这条延迟 NFR 应该落在哪？
q_en: Where should the latency NFR land?
options: 对系统里所有 endpoint 统一要求「应该低延迟」，不区分请求类型地一律压到最低
只对需要显著计算的请求量化，比如搜索 <500ms
延迟不算 NFR，等高层设计时再顺手优化即可
给写入路径设最严延迟目标，因为写通常比读慢
options_en: Put a blanket 'should be low latency' on every endpoint, pushing all requests to the minimum regardless of type.
Quantify only the compute-heavy request — e.g., search under 500ms.
Latency is not an NFR; just optimize it later during high-level design.
Set the strictest latency target on the write path, since writes are usually slower than reads.
why: 延迟 NFR 只对需要显著计算的请求量化（Yelp 搜索 <500ms 是关键），简单读取不必单列目标——否则这句话没有信息量，也指不出真正的瓶颈。代价：你得先判断哪条路径计算最重。
why_en: Quantify latency only for requests doing meaningful computation — e.g., Yelp search under 500ms; a blanket 'be fast' on simple reads carries no signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非功能需求：描述系统品质（可用性/延迟/安全等）而非具体功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An NFR (non-functional requirement) states a system quality like availability, latency, or security rather than a feature.

termDefinitions.meaning: API 端点：一个可被调用的接口地址（如 GET /v1/tweets）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An endpoint is a callable API address, such as GET /v1/tweets.

optionExplanations: 把延迟目标铺满所有接口既做不到也无意义——简单读取本就快，真正的瓶颈是那条计算重的搜索。
对：只给需要显著计算的请求（Yelp 地理搜索）设量化目标，才指出了系统真正的延迟风险点。
延迟是典型 NFR；推迟到高层设计再顺手优化，通常意味着没有目标值，深挖时无从验证。
写路径慢不等于它是延迟关键点；这里用户等的是搜索结果，给写入设目标搞错了对象。
optionExplanations_en: Blanket latency targets on every endpoint are unachievable and meaningless — simple reads are already fast; the search is the risk.
Right — quantify only the compute-heavy request (Yelp's geo-search); that's where the system's real latency risk lives.
Latency is a classic NFR; deferring it to 'optimize later' usually means no target value, so deep dives can't verify it.
A slow write path isn't the latency-critical point here; users wait on search results, so targeting writes aims at the wrong thing.

scenario: 设计一个手机端视频流 App，目标用户常在 3G 网络、设备内存有限、还得省电。
scenario_en: Designing a mobile video-streaming app whose users are often on 3G, with limited device memory, and need to save battery.
q: 这类环境约束最该逼你在设计里做什么取舍？
q_en: What tradeoff should these environment constraints force in your design?
options: 把环境约束当成纯背景信息，认为它不影响架构，直接照搬桌面端的普通设计
按可用带宽自适应码率、克制内存和耗电，让设计迁就受限环境
既然网络差，干脆把全部转码和处理都塞到客户端本地完成
一律按最高清晰度推流，把适配的活儿全丢给客户端
options_en: Treat the constraints as pure background, assume they change nothing, and reuse a plain desktop-grade design.
Use adaptive bitrate to the available bandwidth and restrain memory and battery — bend the design to the constraints.
Since the network is poor, push all transcoding and processing onto the local client.
Stream at the highest quality for everyone and leave the client to cope.
why: 环境约束——手机电池、有限内存、3G 带宽——是硬边界，直接决定码率与缓存策略；设计必须迁就受限设备，而非假设服务器级资源。代价：为弱环境做自适应会抬高复杂度。
why_en: Environment constraints — battery, limited memory, 3G bandwidth — are hard limits that drive bitrate and caching choices; the design must bend to the device.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据当前网络带宽实时切换视频清晰度，避免卡顿。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adaptive bitrate switches video quality in real time based on the current network bandwidth to avoid stalls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第三代移动网络，带宽较低、时延较高的受限网络环境。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 3G is a third-generation mobile network — a low-bandwidth, higher-latency constrained environment.

optionExplanations: 环境约束正是要改变设计的输入：3G/低内存/耗电直接决定码率、缓存和后台策略，不能当背景。
对：受限带宽/内存/电量逼你做自适应码率、瘦客户端等取舍，这就是环境约束落到设计上的样子。
把重活全塞给本已受限的手机，内存和电量先崩——环境约束要减轻客户端负担而非加重。
最高清晰度在 3G 下必然卡顿、耗流量；无视带宽约束正是这条 NFR 想避免的。
optionExplanations_en: Environment constraints are exactly the design input: 3G/low memory/battery drive bitrate, caching, and background policy.
Right — limited bandwidth/memory/battery force adaptive bitrate and a thin client; that's the constraint shaping the design.
Dumping heavy work onto an already-limited phone crashes memory and battery first; constraints should lighten the client.
Top-quality streaming stalls on 3G and burns data; ignoring bandwidth is exactly what this NFR aims to prevent.

scenario: 一个支付网关要求：任何一台机器宕机，交易都不能中断或丢失。你要把「容错」这条 NFR 写具体。
scenario_en: A payment gateway requires that no single machine failure interrupts or drops a transaction. You must make the 'fault tolerance' NFR concrete.
q: 把容错写具体，靠的是哪三个抓手？
q_en: Which three levers make the fault-tolerance NFR concrete?
options: 数据保护、访问控制、合规——但这三条属于「安全」维度，不是容错的抓手
冗余、故障转移、恢复机制——多副本、失效自动切换、崩溃后能重放
把强一致性降成最终一致，换取更高可用性就够了
多做压测、多加日志、多招几个运维顶着
options_en: Data protection, access control, and compliance — but those three are the 'security' dimension, not fault tolerance.
Redundancy, failover, and recovery — replicas, auto-switch on failure, and replay after a crash.
Just downgrade strong consistency to eventual to buy higher availability.
Run more load tests, add more logs, and hire more ops staff.
why: 容错落到三个可设计的抓手：冗余（多副本）、故障转移（失效自动切换）、恢复机制（崩溃后重放）——它们决定单机宕机时系统能否撑住。代价：副本和切换要额外资源与协调。
why_en: Make fault tolerance concrete via three levers: redundancy, failover, and recovery — they decide whether one node's failure takes the whole system down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为关键组件保留多份副本，单份失效时仍有备份顶上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redundancy keeps multiple copies of a critical component so one failure still leaves a working backup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主组件失效时自动把流量切到备用组件，保持服务不中断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failover automatically shifts traffic to a standby component when the primary fails, keeping service up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 副本短期可能不一致，但在没有新写入后最终会收敛到相同值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency lets replicas differ briefly but converge to the same value once writes stop.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：网络分区时只能在一致性与可用性之间二选一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says that under a network partition you must choose between consistency and availability.

optionExplanations: 数据保护/访问控制/合规是「安全」的三抓手，答错了维度——它们防的是攻击与违规，不是宕机。
对：容错=冗余（多副本）+故障转移（失效自动切换）+恢复机制（崩溃后重放），共同扛住宕机。
降一致性换可用是 CAP 取舍，提高的是可用性；它不保证一台宕机时交易不丢，方向不对。
压测/日志/人手是运维手段，能发现问题却不构成容错设计；宕机瞬间靠的是冗余与自动切换。
optionExplanations_en: Data protection/access control/compliance are the three levers of security, not fault tolerance — wrong dimension.
Right — fault tolerance = redundancy (replicas) + failover (auto-switch) + recovery (replay); together they survive a crash.
Trading consistency for availability is a CAP call; it raises availability but doesn't stop a crash from dropping a transaction.
Load tests, logs, and staffing are ops practices that find issues but aren't fault-tolerant design; a crash needs redundancy.

scenario: 你在设计一个存储健康病历的系统，数据高度敏感且受法规约束。你要把「安全」这条 NFR 写具体。
scenario_en: You're designing a system that stores health records — highly sensitive, regulated data. You must make the 'security' NFR concrete.
q: 把安全写具体，该覆盖哪三个方面？
q_en: Which three areas make the security NFR concrete?
options: 冗余、故障转移、恢复机制——但这三条其实是「容错」而非安全的抓手
数据保护、访问控制、合规——加密静态/传输数据、按角色限权、满足法规
只要上了 HTTPS，数据在传输中加密就算安全达标了
把所有数据设为公开只读，反正病历总要给医生看
options_en: Redundancy, failover, and recovery — but those three are really 'fault tolerance', not security.
Data protection, access control, and compliance — encrypt data at rest/in transit, limit by role, meet regulations.
Once HTTPS is on, data is encrypted in transit, so security is covered.
Make all data public read-only — doctors need to see the records anyway.
why: 安全落到三方面：数据保护（加密）、访问控制（按角色限权）、合规（满足法规）——敏感数据系统三条缺一不可。代价：加密和权限校验增加实现与运维成本。
why_en: Make security concrete across data protection (encryption), access control (least privilege), and compliance — a sensitive-data system needs all three.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按身份和角色限制谁能读写哪些数据（最小权限）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Access control restricts who can read or write which data based on identity and role (least privilege).

termDefinitions.meaning: 满足法律法规与行业标准（如数据保护法）的要求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compliance means meeting laws, regulations, and industry standards such as data-protection rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在传输层用 TLS 加密的 HTTP，保护数据在网络传输中不被窃听。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTPS is HTTP encrypted with TLS, protecting data in transit from eavesdropping.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非功能需求：描述系统品质（可用性/延迟/安全等）而非具体功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An NFR (non-functional requirement) states a system quality like availability, latency, or security rather than a feature.

optionExplanations: 冗余/故障转移/恢复是「容错」的抓手，防的是宕机不是泄露——答错了维度。
对：安全=数据保护（加密）+访问控制（限权）+合规（满足法规），病历系统三条都不能少。
HTTPS 只覆盖传输加密，漏了静态数据保护、访问控制和合规——安全远不止一条通道。
公开只读直接放弃访问控制，病历这类敏感数据必然违规泄露，正是安全 NFR 要防的。
optionExplanations_en: Redundancy/failover/recovery are fault-tolerance levers guarding against downtime, not leaks — wrong dimension.
Right — security = data protection (encryption) + access control (least privilege) + compliance; a records system needs all three.
HTTPS covers only transit encryption, missing at-rest protection, access control, and compliance — security is more than one channel.
Public read-only abandons access control; sensitive records would leak and breach regulations — exactly what the NFR prevents.
